requirements.quote:
Servers SHOULD use other contextual information in determining
   priority of requests in the absence of any priority signals.  Servers
requirements.condition: A server determines request priority when no priority signals are present.
requirements.required_behavior: Use other contextual information to determine request priority.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can omit priority signals, supply observable contextual information, and verify that the server uses it in priority selection.

requirements.quote:
MAY interpret the complete absence of signals as an indication that
   the client has not implemented the feature.  The defaults described
requirements.condition: Priority signals are completely absent.
requirements.required_behavior: The server may interpret the absence as indicating that the client has not implemented the feature.
requirements.why_checkable: Server behavior or internal interpretation can be inspected when a client sends no priority signals.

requirements.quote:
It is possible that an endpoint will encounter frames that would
   cause multiple errors.  Implementations MAY discover multiple errors
   during processing, but they SHOULD report at most one stream and one
   connection error as a result.
requirements.condition: Processing frames reveals multiple errors.
requirements.required_behavior: Report at most one stream error and at most one connection error as a result.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reporting more than one stream error or more than one connection error as the result of that processing.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame sequence can trigger multiple errors and emitted stream- and connection-error reports can be counted independently.

requirements.quote:
The first stream error reported for a given stream prevents any other
   errors on that stream from being reported.  In comparison, the
requirements.condition: A stream error has already been reported for a given stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reporting any additional error on that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can induce multiple errors on one stream and verify that only the first is reported.

requirements.quote:
protocol permits multiple GOAWAY frames, though an endpoint SHOULD
   report just one type of connection error unless an error is
   encountered during graceful shutdown.  If this occurs, an endpoint
requirements.condition: An endpoint reports connection errors and no error is encountered during graceful shutdown.
requirements.required_behavior: Report just one type of connection error.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reporting multiple types of connection error outside the graceful-shutdown exception.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection-error reports can be observed and their error types counted while controlling whether graceful shutdown is underway.

requirements.quote:
encountered during graceful shutdown.  If this occurs, an endpoint
   MAY send an additional GOAWAY frame with the new error code, in
   addition to any prior GOAWAY that contained NO_ERROR.
requirements.condition: An error is encountered during graceful shutdown after a prior GOAWAY containing NO_ERROR.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may send an additional GOAWAY carrying the new error code.
requirements.why_checkable: A graceful-shutdown test can induce a later error and inspect whether an additional GOAWAY uses the new error code.

requirements.quote:
If an endpoint detects multiple different errors, it MAY choose to
   report any one of those errors.  If a frame causes a connection
requirements.condition: An endpoint detects multiple different errors.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may select any one of the detected errors to report.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can trigger multiple distinct errors and verify that the selected report corresponds to one of them.

requirements.quote:
report any one of those errors.  If a frame causes a connection
   error, that error MUST be reported.  Additionally, an endpoint MAY
requirements.condition: A frame causes a connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame known to cause a connection error can be injected and the endpoint's error report observed.

requirements.quote:
error, that error MUST be reported.  Additionally, an endpoint MAY
   use any applicable error code when it detects an error condition; a
   generic error code (such as PROTOCOL_ERROR or INTERNAL_ERROR) can
   always be used in place of more specific error codes.
requirements.condition: An endpoint detects an error condition.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may use any applicable error code, including a generic code in place of a more specific code.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Using an error code that is not applicable to the detected condition.
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted error code can be checked for applicability, with generic-code substitution accepted.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that encounters a connection error SHOULD first send a
   GOAWAY frame (Section 6.8) with the stream identifier of the last
   stream that it successfully received from its peer.  The GOAWAY frame
requirements.condition: An endpoint encounters a connection error.
requirements.required_behavior: First send a GOAWAY whose stream identifier identifies the last stream successfully received from the peer.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish the last successfully received peer stream, trigger a connection error, and inspect the first response and GOAWAY stream identifier.

requirements.quote:
stream that it successfully received from its peer.  The GOAWAY frame
   includes an error code (Section 7) that indicates why the connection
   is terminating.  After sending the GOAWAY frame for an error
requirements.condition: A GOAWAY is sent to terminate a connection because of an error.
requirements.required_behavior: Include an error code indicating why the connection is terminating.
requirements.why_checkable: The GOAWAY payload can be decoded and its error code compared with the termination reason.

requirements.quote:
is terminating.  After sending the GOAWAY frame for an error
   condition, the endpoint MUST close the TCP connection.
requirements.condition: An endpoint has sent a GOAWAY for an error condition.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the TCP connection after sending the GOAWAY.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Keeping the TCP connection open after the error GOAWAY.
requirements.why_checkable: The transport state can be observed after transmission of the error GOAWAY.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint can end a connection at any time.  In particular, an
   endpoint MAY choose to treat a stream error as a connection error.
requirements.condition: An endpoint detects a stream error.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may escalate the stream error and treat it as a connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: A stream-error stimulus can be used to verify that connection-error handling is an allowed outcome.

requirements.quote:
endpoint MAY choose to treat a stream error as a connection error.
   Endpoints SHOULD send a GOAWAY frame when ending a connection,
   providing that circumstances permit it.
requirements.condition: An endpoint is ending a connection and circumstances permit sending a frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a GOAWAY frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A controlled connection shutdown can verify whether GOAWAY precedes termination when transmission remains possible.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that detects a stream error sends a RST_STREAM frame
   (Section 6.4) that contains the stream identifier of the stream where
   the error occurred.  The RST_STREAM frame includes an error code that
   indicates the type of error.
requirements.condition: An endpoint detects a stream error.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a RST_STREAM containing the identifier of the stream where the error occurred and an error code indicating the error type.
requirements.why_checkable: A stream error can be induced and the resulting RST_STREAM identifier and error code decoded.

requirements.quote: A RST_STREAM is the last frame that an endpoint can send on a stream.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a RST_STREAM on a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat RST_STREAM as the endpoint's final frame on that stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending any later frame on that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: The endpoint's outbound frame sequence can be monitored for frames after RST_STREAM on the same stream.

requirements.quote:
The peer that sends the RST_STREAM frame MUST be prepared to receive
   any frames that were sent or enqueued for sending by the remote peer.
requirements.condition: An endpoint has sent a RST_STREAM.
requirements.required_behavior: Remain prepared to receive frames already sent or enqueued by the remote peer.
requirements.why_checkable: Frames can be queued before RST_STREAM and delivered afterward to verify that the sender remains able to receive them.

requirements.quote:
any frames that were sent or enqueued for sending by the remote peer.
   These frames can be ignored, except where they modify connection
   state (such as the state maintained for field section compression
   (Section 4.3) or flow control).
requirements.condition: After sending RST_STREAM, an endpoint receives frames that the remote peer had already sent or enqueued.
requirements.required_behavior: Process any such frames that modify connection state, including field-section-compression or flow-control state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Ignoring frames whose effects modify connection state.
requirements.why_checkable: Post-reset frames with known compression or flow-control effects can be delivered and the resulting connection state inspected.

requirements.quote:
Normally, an endpoint SHOULD NOT send more than one RST_STREAM frame
   for any stream.  However, an endpoint MAY send additional RST_STREAM
   frames if it receives frames on a closed stream after more than a
   round-trip time.  This behavior is permitted to deal with misbehaving
   implementations.
requirements.condition: For a stream, unless the endpoint receives frames on that closed stream more than a round-trip time later.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit transmission to at most one RST_STREAM for the stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending more than one RST_STREAM for the stream outside the stated exception.
requirements.why_checkable: RST_STREAM transmissions can be counted while testing both normal operation and the timed closed-stream exception.

requirements.quote:
for any stream.  However, an endpoint MAY send additional RST_STREAM
   frames if it receives frames on a closed stream after more than a
   round-trip time.  This behavior is permitted to deal with misbehaving
   implementations.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives frames on a closed stream more than one round-trip time after closure.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint may send additional RST_STREAM frames for that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A delayed frame can be delivered on a closed stream and additional RST_STREAM transmissions observed.

requirements.quote:
To avoid looping, an endpoint MUST NOT send a RST_STREAM in response
   to a RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives a RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Sending a RST_STREAM in response to the received RST_STREAM.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can send RST_STREAM and verify that no responsive RST_STREAM is emitted.

requirements.quote:
If the TCP connection is closed or reset while streams remain in the
   "open" or "half-closed" states, then the affected streams cannot be
   automatically retried (see Section 8.7 for details).
requirements.condition: The TCP connection is closed or reset while streams remain open or half-closed.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection can be terminated with streams in each named state and automatic retry behavior observed.

requirements.quote:
additional services or alter any aspect of the protocol.  Extensions
   are effective only within the scope of a single HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 protocol extension is in use.
requirements.required_behavior: Confine the extension's effects to a single HTTP/2 connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allowing extension state or effects to carry automatically across HTTP/2 connections.
requirements.why_checkable: Separate connections can be established and checked for leakage of extension state or effects.

requirements.quote:
Implementations MUST ignore unknown or unsupported values in all
   extensible protocol elements.  Implementations MUST discard frames
requirements.condition: An implementation encounters an unknown or unsupported value in an extensible protocol element.
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the unknown or unsupported value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Acting on the value as though it were known and supported.
requirements.why_checkable: Unknown values can be injected into extensible elements and their effect on processing observed.

requirements.quote:
extensible protocol elements.  Implementations MUST discard frames
   that have unknown or unsupported types.  This means that any of these
requirements.condition: An implementation receives a frame with an unknown or unsupported type.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard the frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Processing the frame as a supported frame type.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame with an unrecognized type can be sent and the implementation checked for discard behavior.

requirements.quote:
arrangement or negotiation.  However, extension frames that appear in
   the middle of a field block (Section 4.3) are not permitted; these
   MUST be treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: An extension frame appears in the middle of a field block.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Permitting the extension frame within the field block.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the condition as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: An extension frame can be inserted between field-block fragments and the resulting connection-level PROTOCOL_ERROR observed.
